label: verify --skill <name> exit 1 is the documented expected state: the standard defines gate as the enforced presence+format check and verify as a reconciliation tool reporting accumulated drift; observed verify sk-code = 340 mismatches exit 1 while the same skill's corpus wrapper gate exits 0

The derivation is self-invalidating by construction: W = min(realEditCount(file),99) is a git-history function, applying W is itself an edit, so one pass never converges and stored==derived is transient absent two-pass apply+amend or same-commit apply discipline

The derivation is faithful; stored values are stale mint-epoch snapshots: stack-detection.md shows 28 path-commits, expected W=26, stored 2.2.0.0; other stored values carry nonzero Z (sk-code/README.md 2.2.11.0 vs expected 2.2.0.38) and pre-anchor-move values (1.5.0.x vs 2.2.0.y)

Enforcement covers presence+format only on three surfaces (post-edit hook runs gate scoped by skill; quick_validate/package_skill reject malformed/absent at package time; CI runs a different frontmatter-coverage guard); none compares stored vs derived, and apply skips differing values without --update

The standard's 'Run it in CI or pre-commit' instruction for the corpus gate is unhonored: a searched surface (.github/workflows, .githooks, package.json) shows no wiring of check-frontmatter-versions.sh or frontmatter-version.mjs, and even honored the gate would not catch value drift because it is presence+format only
The engine is duplicated byte-for-byte across scripts/ and shared/scripts/ (diff -q clean) while the standard links only the shared/scripts copy, doubling the update surface for drift-sensitive logic

Composite answer to Q1: rule and derivation are functioning; what is absent is any enforcement of stored-vs-derived equality, so exit 1 on nearly every skill is guaranteed until a skill is two-pass reconciled and left untouched - the real question is what property the stored per-doc version should assert (feeds Q2-Q4)
